title: Extraction of 1-HP Derivatives and HPLC Preparation
author: Muhammad Zaka Asif

steps.title: Remove lyophilized sample
steps.instruction: Take the dried sample out of the lyophilizer; it should appear as a powder.

steps.title: Resuspend and vortex in methanol
steps.instruction: Add the minimal amount of methanol needed to fully submerge the pellet, then vortex the tube to aid dissolution.

substeps.instruction: Add enough methanol to cover the pellet.
Vortex until the pellet appears dissolved.

steps.title: Minimize solution volume for injection
steps.instruction: Keep the final solution volume as low as possible because the HPLC injector caps at 90 µL, reducing the number of injections required.

steps.title: Centrifuge solution
steps.instruction: Transfer the methanol suspension to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 20,800 RCF for 30 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Place the suspension in a 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to HPLC tubes
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette only the clear supernatant into HPLC sample tubes, avoiding any solids, and record the volume to ensure accurate injection.

substeps.instruction: Avoid disturbing the pellet at the tube bottom.
Note the transferred volume for injection calculations.

steps.title: Load tubes and run HPLC
steps.instruction: Place the HPLC tubes in the correct loading sites of the HPLC instrument and start the predefined run protocol.

steps.title: Collect and store fractions
steps.instruction: During the HPLC run, collect fractions (manually or automatically); after collection, store them at –80 °C for later NMR preparation.
